newsitem.title: CANADA: Alberta oil play may get real test after 4 years.
newsitem.headline: Alberta oil play may get real test after 4 years.

text.p: Partners in Alberta's Moose Mountain oil play in Alberta will finally get the opportunity to test wells drilled there if regulators approve a pipeline plan which was announced on Friday, the head of one of the firms said.
"Initially, this is going to be an extended production test," Rigel Energy Corp chief executive Don West said in a phone interview. "We don't know what we've got and it could be a whole lot."

Husky Oil Operations Ltd, operator of the play, said it and Rigel applied to Alberta's Energy and Utilities board to build a 25 km pipeline to connect two wells to Shell Canada Ltd's Jumping Pound Gas Plant in the southwest Alberta.

The Moose Mountain discovery, made four years ago in Alberta's craggy, environmentally sensitive Kananaskis Country west of Calgary, created a buzz in Canada's oil patch over what looked like a major oil and natural gas find.

But the partners were frustrated by fruitless attempts to test the wells using unconventional methods because of the region's mountainous terrain, ecological concerns and strong opposition from environmental groups.
Five wells -- four oil and one gas -- have been drilled on the play, but the size of the reserves and potential production remain unknown.
"We've never got a decent test. This will determine it, " West said. "We will look at an extended test for probably three to six months and we'll evaluate after that."
The evaluation would determine whether to drill more wells and expand the capacity of the pipeline, which was initially expected to cost C$12 million.
Husky has two-thirds working interest in Moose Mountain and Rigel has the remainder. Jordan Petroleum recently acquired Transwest Energy Inc, which has an overriding royalty on Rigel's stake.
West said that the partners expect to reap at least a return on investment from the 950 barrel per day pipeline through the exercise.

"I think the key thing is that we're finally getting it on production and that we will have a decent test once we get the pipeline built. Then we'll know from there what size of situation we have and just how we'll develop it," he said.
Analysts have said Rigel's stock price has not reflected the potential value from Moose Mountain for years. Its stock closed down 0.10 on Friday to 13.50.
